raw_provider_output.summary: IBM's 'Smarter Cities' campaign uses interactive, functional street furniture to demonstrate how smart technology can seamlessly integrate into daily urban life.

observations.description: A man sits on a bench that is part of a large orange billboard. The bench is functional, and the billboard displays the text 'Smart Ideas for Smarter Cities' and the IBM logo.
A person stands under a blue billboard that has a striped awning. Rain is falling, and the awning is providing shelter, turning the advertisement into a functional shelter.
A woman with a rolling suitcase walks up a set of stairs. A teal billboard extends from the wall to form a ramp, allowing her to roll her luggage up the steps.
The text 'Smart Ideas for Smarter Cities' is repeated across all three installations, accompanied by the IBM logo and a URL (people.smartercities.com).
The advertisements are placed in real-world urban environments (sidewalks, stairs) and are designed to be used by the public, blurring the line between advertising and public infrastructure.

claims.text: The core message is that IBM's technology can solve practical urban problems by making the city 'smarter' and more user-friendly.

The ad uses the physical transformation of the billboard into a functional object (bench, shelter, ramp) as a visual metaphor for how technology should work: invisibly and usefully within the environment.
By providing a tangible benefit (shelter from rain, a place to sit, a way to move luggage), the ad uses the principle of reciprocity to create a positive association with the brand.
The target audience is urban dwellers and commuters who interact with city infrastructure daily and value convenience and innovation.
